questionText: How do you configure the embedded Tomcat in Spring Boot?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can configure common and Tomcat-specific properties, distinguish connections, pending queue, workers, and timeout meanings, and tune from measurements.
inScope: Connection, accept queue, and worker limits
outOfScope: Treating connection-timeout as a controller execution deadline
prerequisites: Basic HTTP connection and request idea

claims.statement: Spring Boot exposes common server properties under server.* and Tomcat-specific settings under server.tomcat.*.
max-connections, accept-count, and threads.max govern distinct connection, pending-queue, and worker resources.
server.tomcat.connection-timeout waits after connection acceptance for the request URI line, while keep-alive-timeout waits for another request on a persistent connection.

examples.title: Tomcat port, worker, connection, queue, and timeout properties

validation.command: Focused embedded-server example gate parses every property key, integer, and duration
validation.expected: All documented keys and illustrative values parse and no value is presented as a universal recommendation

visuals.title: Connection cap, pending queue, request line, worker, and controller flow

notes: Illustrative capacity values are clearly labelled for load-test validation.

review.notes: Property names and semantics were checked against Spring Boot 3.3 common application properties; the answer explicitly separates connector timeouts from controller and downstream deadlines.
